newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus-Russia to publish integration charter.
newsitem.headline: Belarus-Russia to publish integration charter.

text.p: Belarus and Russia said on Tuesday they had put the finishing touches to a charter outlining measures to integrate their two states and that it was ready to go forward for public discussion.

Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and visiting Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said they had agreed the final text of the charter on Monday and that it would appear in the press on Wednesday.
"Yesterday we agreed not just last proposals but the last word on this charter," Lukashenko said.

According to a memorandum initialled along with the charter by Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin last week, the finalised charter should now go up for more than a month of public discussion and possible amendment.
The two presidents also signed a Union Treaty, but after a last-minute diplomatic scramble, it ended up largely symbolic, with all the details transfered into the embryonic charter.

The issue of integration, favoured by the smaller and poorer Belarus, is a source of huge controversy in Moscow, where liberals fear a drain on the economy and the possibility that the hardline Lukashenko might win a say over Russian affairs.

Lukashenko is determined that the two countries unite, although he has not made clear what that would involve. "Since the supporters are immeasurably more numerous than the opponents of our unity, the supporters will anyhow win," Lukashenko said.
His foreign minister, Ivan Antonovich, said a union would not mean a loss of sovereignity for Belarus.
"The formula "one country -- one voice" in the context of the union will be reflected as "two countries -- two voices, two equal sovereign states," he said.
